rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists worship powerless things despite God's power and wisdom; polytheism is disbelief.
rows.anchor: Yet these foolish people are worshipping

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic noun refers to the previously mentioned polytheists, since polytheism is disbelief.
rows.anchor: The word M is used as a generic noun and refers to the polytheists

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for helper means rival with ʿalā; the polytheists aid Satan against God and oppose the messenger's monotheist call.
rows.anchor: meaning of rival is incorporated in it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must deliver warnings and glad tidings and explain denial's consequences; acceptance or rejection is people's responsibility, not his.
rows.anchor: his responsibility is only to deliver warnings and glad tidings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People alone benefit from following the way or bear its consequences; neither outcome harms the Prophet.
rows.anchor: those who trust God are never deprived of His blessings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trust in the living God brings blessings, with a subtle taunt that idols can neither benefit nor harm.
rows.anchor: There also exists a subtle sarcasm in it on the dead deities of the idolaters

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorifying God with gratitude is a means to patience and trust; Qur'anic calls to patience and trust also direct the Prophet to prayer.
rows.anchor: the means of attaining patience and trust

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The six days are God's days, whose length only He knows; they may be understood as six phases, showing deliberate rather than accidental creation.
rows.anchor: For our understanding, we can regard them to be six phases

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ascent to the throne means He did not become detached after creating the universe; He governs it, and its evolution follows His plan.
rows.anchor: after creating this universe in this way God did not become aloof from it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raḥmān is a predicate with its subject suppressed for emphasis; it presents creation as purposeful and merciful, entailing a day when mercy appears with perfect justice.
rows.anchor: whose inchoative (mubtadā’) is suppressed. The sentence is to the effect:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should ask the one who truly knows God's attributes rather than inventing them; God teaches His reality through His book and messenger.
rows.anchor: instead, they should consult Him Who knows His attributes the most.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition with the verb “ask” would imply mockery only in another usage; that sense does not apply here.
rows.anchor: Here this cannot be the case. God has referred to His own self here

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God knows opponents' sins, the Prophet should consign their case to Him, and the verse directs people to seek attributes from one who knows.
rows.anchor: the Prophet (sws) should consign the matter of his opponents to God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The refusal to prostrate before the Most Merciful is especially perverse because al-Raḥmān is the Creator's greatest attribute.
rows.anchor: The greatest attribute of the creator of the heavens and the earth is

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh exploited al-Raḥmān's greater familiarity among People of the Book, contrasting it with Allah among Arabian idolaters, to claim Jewish authorship and incite religious and national resentment.
rows.anchor: the former name was more common among the People of the Book

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an warns that prejudice against al-Raḥmān deprives people of the blessings contained in this divine name.
rows.anchor: this name of God is a treasure trove of His immense blessings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the sūrah's close, attention returns from address to worldly signs: there is no shortage of signs, but people need the will to benefit from them.
rows.anchor: these verses at the end once again direct attention to the signs found in the world around human beings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reminder addresses the intellect and gratitude the heart; signs throughout creation sustain both, but benefiting from them depends on intention, which God tests without coercing human choice.
rows.anchor: “Reminder” relates to the intellect and “gratitude” to the heart.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavenly stations or posts set limits that prevent devils among jinn and humans from reaching the realm of revelation; angels guard them and carry revelation to prophets.
rows.anchor: It refers to the stations and posts created by God in this universe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since revelation is the only access to the unseen, soothsayers, astrologers, and other claimants to unseen knowledge are liars.
rows.anchor: There is no other means except this to find the news of the unseen world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah and this arrangement both begin with “blessed”; divine blessing entails protecting revelation from satanic intrusion because spiritual life and success depend on it.
rows.anchor: This points to the fact that it is the necessary consequence of God being “blessed”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding passage portrays the traits of God's people, whose living intellect and heart let them benefit from His signs and Book, in contrast to those opposing the Prophet.
rows.anchor: the Almighty has enumerated the traits and qualities of His people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accounts of earlier peoples corroborate that God tests truth-seekers, divine rights outrank kinship obligations, and persecutors cannot escape God's grasp.
rows.anchor: It is an established practice of the Almighty to test people who tread the path of the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spider-web parable depicts the fragile schemes of God's adversaries and the baselessness of their deities and intercessors.
rows.anchor: the parable of the schemes of such people is like that of the web of a spider.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world has a wise purpose; the Prophet should recite God's Book and persist in prayer through adversity, which is a haven and source of strength for believers.
rows.anchor: This world is not a place of amusement and sport for children.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage answers objections from the People of the Book about Muḥammad's prophethood, guides Muslim debate, praises good People of the Book, and answers demands for a miracle.
rows.anchor: Some objections raised by the People of the Book on the prophethood of Muḥammad

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those demanding that the Prophet hasten the torment receive a response.
rows.anchor: Those who were demanding from the Prophet (sws) to hasten the torment are responded to.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims harassed for professing faith are instructed to migrate and promised success in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: Muslims who were being harassed because of the crime of professing faith are directed to migrate

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The close argues for monotheism from facts idolaters acknowledge, rebukes their ingratitude for the Baytullāh's protection and prosperity, depicts consequences, and consoles believers with God's help.
rows.anchor: An argument is cited in favour of monotheism from established facts acknowledged by the idolaters.

none: Verse text and translation with section headings only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alif Lām Mīm is the name of this sūrah; its discussion has already appeared under al-Baqarah.
rows.anchor: Research on this has already been presented in Sūrah al-Baqarah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general wording refers in context to Makkan converts shaken by persecution: they expected an easy path, developed doubts, and risked hypocrisy because they had not understood the trials of truth.
rows.anchor: the reference is to people who had become worried in the trying circumstances of Makkah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A claim to faith alone does not make someone a believer without the test of trial; the passage addresses people who wrongly expected to avoid difficulty.
rows.anchor: merely on the basis of this claim they will be regarded as believers without putting them through trial.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As earlier messengers and their followers were tested, current claimants to faith must also be tested; trials distinguish the truthful from wrongdoers, and “know” means distinguish.
rows.anchor: the way such people who lived before them were put into trials, they too will face trials.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensive form of “know” emphasizes that testing is God's established practice, which people cannot avoid.
rows.anchor: the word  علم  is used in its intensive form.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God fully knows each person's sincerity or hypocrisy, He rewards and punishes on the basis of deeds; trials determine people's standing.
rows.anchor: He does not punish or reward people merely on the basis of His knowledge

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning targets persecutors of weak Muslims who mistake God's respite for indifference or inability to seize them; their judgment of God is wrong.
rows.anchor: it actually refers to the wicked people who were persecuting Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Oppressed Muslims should keep the Hereafter in view and trust that their appointed meeting with God will bring reward for their work and trials; God knows their sacrifices and their enemies' terror.
rows.anchor: the time for its arrival is prescribed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears and knows all, including oppressed Muslims' sacrifices and the terror imposed by their enemies.
rows.anchor: He is fully aware of their sacrifices and also cognizant of the reign of terror

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Striving in God's cause benefits the believer, not God; religious practice, like a farmer's labor, is prescribed for human well-being, so calamity should not cause anxiety.
rows.anchor: when a person treads the path of religion he alone is to gain and not God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Context indicates that “sins” here means minor sins; God removes them from believers who do righteous deeds and abundantly rewards all their deeds.
rows.anchor: It is evidence from the placement and context that the word تٰاِّیَس refers to minor sins.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many trials for new converts came from disbelieving fathers and guardians who invoked parental rights to obstruct duties to God; this resembles ordeals faced by Abraham, Moses' followers, and early Muslims.
rows.anchor: the tough times the newly converted youth would face from their fathers and guardians who were disbelievers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage turns from the previous verse's warning to glad tidings for believers who remain steadfast in faith and righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: The previous verse had a strong ring of warning in it. This verse has a strong ring of glad tidings in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human harm in this world is brief compared with God's eternal punishment, so bearing even great calamities for truth is preferable to abandoning it.
rows.anchor: whatever harm a person receives in this world is very short as compared to God’s torment which will eternally seize them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their present trials have shaken some claimants enough to join God's enemies in complaining about what has happened to them.
rows.anchor: at this time trials have really jolted them and they have joined the enemies of God in complaining of what has befallen them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who persist in faith and righteous deeds despite enmity will be admitted among the sincere and pure, whom God selects for His eternal kingdom through trials.
rows.anchor: Only those will be regarded its part who will pass in the trials they endure.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human harm is a temporary trial, unlike eternal divine punishment; one must withstand oppression for truth or choose evil and face loss, with no third path.
rows.anchor: There is no other option than these two.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source calls worldly harm from people fitna because it is a test, while Hereafter punishment is God's inescapable torment.
rows.anchor: the harm a person faces from people is called ۃَنۡتِف  trial).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some shaken claimants later claim solidarity and sacrifices when divine help appears, though God knows what is in their hearts.
rows.anchor: when later the signs of God’s help appear they will emphatically say

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Claims of solidarity cannot fool God, who knows the secrets of people's hearts.
rows.anchor: But how can it succeed before someone who knows people inside out.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will sift sincere believers from hypocrites; the believers are sincere followers, unlike claimants unwilling to face hardship, and justice requires this distinction.
rows.anchor: If He does not do this, it will be against His justice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers pressured converted dependents to follow them and promised to bear their sins, a tactic used by elders and leaders; religious responsibility is individual, so blind following or coercion is forbidden.
rows.anchor: The Almighty has made each person individually answerable for it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can carry another person's burden before God, as the Qur'an explicitly states.
rows.anchor: None will be able to bear the burden of another person before God.
